answer: Fix the emission pool per epoch and pay it only for graded original work: the tide is the same size no matter how many hands reach for it. Park new identities in a throttled lagoon - low caps, vested payouts - until their answers survive peer grading. A sybil farm then splits one fixed tide across many quarantined seats while paying linear inference cost per seat, and duplicate-answer detection slashes correlated accounts. Faking a crowd in this ocean costs more than the crowd can earn.
